color.definition.question: How is the palette defined?
color.definition.why: True neutrals and blue 600 as the brand: the familiar web color of links and focus, AAA with white text, and clear to color-blind users.

typography.definition.question: How are sizes and line heights defined?
typography.definition.answer: A ratio, line heights in proportion
typography.definition.why: Line height grows with text size for zoom users.

typography.values.question: How large is body text?
typography.values.why: Large text is readable for more people.

shape.definition.question: How are corners set?
shape.definition.why: One brand, one set of corners.

elevation.definition.question: What separates groups on the page?
elevation.definition.why: Strong borders separate groups at any zoom.

elevation.values.question: How soft are shadows?
elevation.values.why: No shadows; borders do the work.

motion.definition.question: How is easing defined?
motion.definition.why: A standard ease-out is easy to follow.

motion.values.question: How fast does feedback feel?
motion.values.why: Moderate speed is easy to follow.

accessibility.values.question: What is the smallest target?
accessibility.values.why: Large targets for tremor and touch.

people.q2.question: What accessibility level do we commit to?
people.q2.why: AAA where it applies; nobody is left out.

people.q1.question: Who uses it most?
people.q1.why: Everyone, including people with low vision, motor and cognitive needs.

business.q1.question: What does the product do for the business?
business.q1.why: A public service everyone must be able to use.

accessibility.roles.question: Which states get their own visible value?
accessibility.roles.why: Every state, including loading, gets its own value.

human.q1.question: What must the interface protect?
human.q1.why: Low effort to understand each step.

brand.q1.question: What should the brand feel like?

brand.q3.question: Which typefaces carry the product, and why?
brand.q3.why: Atkinson Hyperlegible for everything: it was drawn so letters can't be mistaken, and nobody is left out.

content.q1.question: What is the main content?
content.q1.why: Most screens are forms and steps.

content.q2.question: How much is on one screen?
content.q2.why: One question per screen lowers effort.

outcomes.q2.question: What is a costly mistake?
outcomes.q2.why: A failed form can cost someone a benefit.

typography.lands.question: Where does type do the most work?
typography.lands.why: Type matters most in form labels and hints.

typography.count.question: How many steps does the type scale take?
typography.count.answer: Only the steps the screens need

shape.count.question: How many corner sizes exist?
shape.count.why: Control, badge and container corners differ.

elevation.roles.question: What rises above the page?
elevation.roles.why: Flat is easier to read at high zoom.

iconography.count.question: How many icon sizes exist?
iconography.count.why: One size, larger than the text.

iconography.values.question: How big are icons next to text?
iconography.values.why: Larger icons are easier to see.

spacing.roles.question: Which spacing roles does it need?
spacing.roles.why: Large rows matter for touch and zoom.

outcomes.q1.question: Which outcome matters most?
outcomes.q1.why: Completion without errors is the measure.

color.count.question: How many emphasis levels do actions need?
color.count.why: Primary and secondary only; fewer choices, fewer errors.

accessibility.count.question: How many signals carry each meaning?

color.lands.why: Links and actions must be found by everyone.

border-width.default.why: We use a 2px default line for borders and dividers in order to give separation and grouping that hold at any zoom. A heavier stroke does this by keeping the edge visible where a 1px line fades. So people with low vision still find each group, because strong lines separate groups (elevation.definition) and text holds AAA (accessibility.definition).

border-width.focus-offset.why: We use a fixed 2px focus offset in order to keep focus visible by contrast, not for style. The gap does this by showing the page color between ring and control, so one of the two colors keeps enough contrast against any fill (W3C technique C40). So people see the ring on any fill and at any zoom, because every state has its own look (accessibility.roles).
border-width.focus-offset.description: The gap between a control and its focus ring, so the ring never touches the control and reads on any fill.

border-width.focus.why: We use a 3px focus ring in order to show focus, one step heavier than the 2px default line by the focus relation. A heavier stroke does this by standing out even from the strong borders around it. So everyone sees where the keyboard is, because every state has its own look (accessibility.roles) and lines are strong (elevation.definition).

motion.duration.feedback.why: Moderate speed is easy to follow.
motion.duration.feedback.description: Feedback speed: moderate. Hover, press and small state changes.

motion.duration.panels.why: A moderate open is easy to follow and shows where the panel came from.
motion.duration.panels.description: Panel speed: moderate. Dialogs, sheets, popovers and menus opening and closing. One speed: panels open at the feedback speed (motion.count).

motion.easing.standard.why: A plain ease-out is calm and clear. An overshoot can confuse and distract.

type.title.line-height.why: Title lines are 1.25 times its 28px size, 35px, the same tight ratio as display, and they grow with the text on zoom.

type.heading.line-height.why: Heading lines are 1.25 times its 22px size, 27.5px: the smallest role on the tight ratio, while text from 19px down takes 1.6.

type.body.line-height.why: Body lines are 1.6 times its 19px size, 30.4px: the open ratio for paragraphs, so short lines of large text lower effort.

type.caption.line-height.why: Caption lines are 1.6 times its 16px size, 25.6px: the smallest text keeps the open ratio and grows with the text on zoom.

type.data.line-height.why: Data lines match body, 1.6 times 19px, 30.4px, so numbers in a table read with the same room as text.

type.caption.font-size.why: Caption is the smallest step, 16px, exactly 1rem: even secondary text never drops below the reader's own default size.

type.label.font-size.why: Label is 18px, one pixel under body, because form labels and hints are where type matters most.

type.body.font-size.why: Body is 19px, three pixels above the 16px caption, because large text is readable for more people.

type.data.font-size.why: Data uses the 19px body size, not a small or mono size, because every number must be readable at large size.

type.heading.font-size.why: Heading is 22px, a clear step between the 28px title and the 19px body, so a section inside a form step stands out.

type.title.font-size.why: Title is 28px, one clear step below display, and the same on every page, so people always know where they are.

type.display.font-size.why: Display is the largest step, 36px, kept off page titles: it changes from page to page and pushes the content down.

type.body.font-weight.why: Body is regular, 400, the plain weight for paragraphs; bold stays for the roles that mark structure.

type.caption.font-weight.why: Caption is regular, 400, not bold: it carries secondary text, and the scheme loads only regular and bold.

type.data.font-weight.why: Data is regular, 400, like body, so numbers in a table read as plain content and not as labels.

type.display.font-weight.why: Display is bold, 700, one of the two weights the scheme loads; bold and the 36px size together mark the top of the page.

type.title.font-weight.why: Title is bold, 700, so the 28px page title reads as a heading and never as large body text.

type.heading.font-weight.why: Heading is bold, 700: at 22px it sits only 3px above body, so weight, not size alone, sets it apart.

type.label.font-weight.why: Label is bold, 700: at 18px it is close to the body size, so bold marks it as the field's always visible label.

opacity.disabled.why: It comes with a hint that says what is missing. People must learn why they cannot go on. The hint tells them the next step.

radius.badge.why: We use a 4px corner for badges and checkboxes in order to give marks a role of their own, apart from the 6px controls. The smallest radius does this by keeping a clear rectangle around a word or a check. So a status never looks like a pill button, because badges get their own corner (shape.roles) and the brand is clear (brand.q1).
radius.badge.description: Corner of badges, chips, tooltips, keyboard keys (kbd) and checkboxes: small labels and marks.

radius.option.why: We use a 4px corner for menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 8px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by following the outer curve at the padding's distance. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because surfaces take 8px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).
radius.option.description: Corner of options in menus and lists: the panel's corner less its padding, so the corners nest.

radius.control.why: We use a 6px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a calm, clear tone, by brand convention. A slight radius does this by softening the edge while the box keeps a clear rectangle. So every field and button reads plainly as something to use, because the brand is calm and clear (brand.q1) and corners are slightly rounded (shape.values).

radius.element.why: We use the 6px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a text area or a list row the curve of the fields beside it. So people see one family of boxes on a form, because the control corner is slight, not a pill (shape.values), and the brand is clear (brand.q1).
radius.element.description: Corner of an element that holds content and can grow past one line: a list item, an accordion row, a text area, a calendar, an attachment, a skeleton or media.

radius.surface.why: We use an 8px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. The largest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 6px controls inside it. So a step card reads as one object that holds its fields, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is calm and clear (brand.q1).
radius.surface.description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

elevation.card.why: We use no shadow for cards in order to keep them at the page's height: the scale gives no layer a step here. The missing shade does this by leaving the card flat, framed by a strong line. So the page stays easy to read at high zoom, because nothing rises (elevation.roles) and there are no shadows (elevation.values).

elevation.overlay.why: We use no shadow for menus and dialogs in order to show their height without a cast shade: the scale gives no layer a step here. The missing shade does this by leaving the layer to its border and the dimmed page behind it. So a dialog stands out at any zoom with no blur to read through, because nothing rises (elevation.roles) and there are no shadows (elevation.values).

size.icon.why: One icon size, 20px, one step larger than the 19px body text it sits beside, so every icon stays easy to see.

size.control.compact.why: It still meets the large target size and fits inside the field.

size.control.default.why: Large targets help people with motor needs.
size.control.default.description: Height of buttons and inputs, and the smallest target.

size.control.large.why: It is the same height as the default here. Every control is already large. One height on every button keeps pages predictable.
size.control.large.description: Height of large controls. Not used in this system, so it equals the default.

size.row.why: Large rows are easy to read and tap.

space.gap.tight.why: Parts sit close enough to read as one item, with room to tell them apart at high zoom.

space.gap.default.why: Items in one group sit 16px apart, not the 12px tight gap: generous space between fields stops mis-taps.

space.inset.cell-x.why: Clear space between columns keeps values apart at high zoom.

component-spacing-map.hairline.why: hairline: A fixed 2px optical nudge, the same in every scheme. Spacious: space lowers effort and mis-taps, so components get the most room short of the brand scheme; rows stay tight.

space.inset.control-x.why: Wide padding makes each button a bigger target that is easy to hit.
